1 Introduction

This vignette compares the selection diagnostic side-by-side across two choices of selection_rule, holding all other ForestSearch parameters fixed. It uses the package’s compare_selection_rules() wrapper to run forestsearch() once per combination and bundle the per-combo diagnostics for inspection.

The structure is:

  1. Data setup + ITT — identical to the single-rule analyses.
  2. Comparison run — one call to compare_selection_rules() that handles the loop, captures each run’s CANDIDATE EVALUATION PREVIEW + CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY banners, builds the Pareto-frontier plots, and computes split-derived CIs.
  3. Per-combo diagnostics — replay of captured console output, individual frontier plot/table/narrative for each combination.
  4. Side-by-side composition — patchwork-composed plot panel for direct visual comparison.

Bootstrap, cross-validation, and the combined forest plot are deliberately omitted so the document stays focused on the selection mechanism and the comparison reads as a tight diagnostic of the rule axis alone.

2 Setup

2.1 Load Required Packages

Code 
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(forestsearch)
  library(speff2trial)       # ACTG175 dataset
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gt)
  library(future)
  library(patchwork)         # for side-by-side plot composition
})

# Source the comparison wrapper.  When this graduates into the package
# (copy compare_selection_rules.R into R/ and run devtools::document()),
# this source() line can be removed.
#source("compare_selection_rules.R")

# Set ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

2.2 Analysis Parameters

All ForestSearch parameters are defined here once and reused for both combinations. The two axes of variation are sg_focus and selection_rule, which the wrapper handles directly.

# ─── Parallel processing ────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_cores <- max(1L, floor(0.95 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))

# ─── Reproducibility ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
analysis_seed <- 8316951L
set.seed(analysis_seed)

# ─── Confounders ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")
confounders.name <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)
id.name <- "id"

# ─── Variables (dual-scale framing) ────────────────────────────────────
treat.name         <- "treat"
adverse_outcome    <- "y_decline"   # FS adverse-scale outcome
beneficial_outcome <- "y_improve"   # GRF beneficial-scale outcome

# ─── ForestSearch parameters (continuous, MD scale) ────────────────────
fs_outcome_type    <- "continuous"
fs_effect_measure  <- "MD"

# NOTE: fs_sg_focus and fs_selection_rule are NOT defined here.
# They live in the `comparison-axes` chunk below as the two axes the
# wrapper varies.  All OTHER ForestSearch parameters are fixed across
# the comparison.

# Thresholds in CD4 count units (adverse scale: MD > c1 = harm)
fs_md_threshold    <- 10    # screening: MD >= 10 indicates harm
fs_md_consistency  <- 5     # consistency: MD >= 5

fs_pconsistency    <- 0.90
fs_n_min           <- 60L
fs_d0_min          <- 10L
fs_d1_min          <- 10L
fs_splits          <- 500L

fs_max_subgroups   <- 30

fs_maxk            <- 2L
fs_use_lasso       <- TRUE
fs_use_grf         <- TRUE
fs_is_RCT          <- TRUE
fs_vi_grf_min      <- -0.2
fs_dmin_grf        <- 0
fs_cont_cutoff     <- 4L

# ─── Pareto-frontier diagnostic parameters ──────────────────────────────
frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits      = 1000L,
  seed          = 1L,
  xlim          = NULL,
  digits        = 2L
)

# ─── Output directory for saved artifacts ───────────────────────────────
# .rds bundles (tidy selected-subgroups + full comparison object) are
# written by the "Selected Subgroups" section below.  Resolved relative
# to *this qmd's directory*, not the caller's getwd() -- so the path is
# the same whether the chunk is rendered by Quarto or executed
# interactively from a different working directory.  Created if it
# doesn't exist.  Matches the calibration-suite convention.
#
# Resolution: knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE) returns the full path
# of the input document during a render; NULL otherwise.  When NULL
# (e.g., interactive chunk execution), fall back to getwd(), which
# matches Quarto's behavior of cd'ing to the qmd's directory before
# rendering chunks.
qmd_input  <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
qmd_dir    <- if (is.null(qmd_input)) getwd() else dirname(qmd_input)
output_dir <- file.path(qmd_dir, "_data")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

2.3 Comparison Axes

The two axes varied by the wrapper. Tuple semantics: paired element-by-element.

Note

sg_focus = "effMaxSG" notation. The "eff*" names ("eff", "effMaxSG", "effMinSG") are GLM-natural aliases for the legacy Cox-flavored names ("hr", "hrMaxSG", "hrMinSG"). Both vocabularies produce identical results. The "eff*" forms read more naturally for continuous (MD), binary (OR/RR/RD), and count (IRR) outcomes where there is no hazard ratio. Old code using "hrMaxSG" continues to work without changes.

Code 
sg_focus_vec       <- c("effMaxSG", "effMaxSG", "effMinSG", "effMinSG", "eff", "maxSG","minSG")
selection_rule_vec <- c("pareto",   "both", "pareto", "both", "neighborhood", "neighborhood", "neighborhood")

# Pretty labels used in plot titles, list names, and prose
combo_labels       <- paste(sg_focus_vec, selection_rule_vec, sep = " / ")
n_combos           <- length(sg_focus_vec)

cat("Combinations to be run:\n")
Combinations to be run:
Code 
print(data.frame(
  combo          = seq_len(n_combos),
  sg_focus       = sg_focus_vec,
  selection_rule = selection_rule_vec,
  label          = combo_labels
))

3 Data Preparation

3.1 Treatment Assignment

Code 
# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

3.2 Outcome Construction

Code 
# Drop subjects missing the week-20 CD4 measurement
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# Adverse scale: CD4 decline (higher = worse)
actg_df$y_decline <- actg_df$cd40 - actg_df$cd420

outcome_vars <- c("y_decline")

3.3 Covariates

Code 
# Coerce binary indicators to factors (analyst does not know true cuts
# for continuous covariates; ForestSearch handles those internally)
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.factor(actg_df[[v]])

cat("Continuous candidates:", paste(cont_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
Continuous candidates: age, preanti, wtkg, karnof, cd40, cd80

4 Selection-Rule Comparison

4.1 Running compare_selection_rules()

One call to the wrapper runs forestsearch() for each (sg_focus, selection_rule) combination with all other parameters held fixed, and bundles the per-combo diagnostics into a single object.

Code 
t0 <- proc.time()

comparison <- compare_selection_rules(
  df.analysis      = actg_df,
  sg_focus         = sg_focus_vec,
  selection_rule   = selection_rule_vec,
  combo_labels     = combo_labels,

  # Wrapper-specific controls
  compute_cis      = TRUE,
  n_splits         = frontier_params$n_splits,
  ci_seed          = frontier_params$seed,
  plot_xlim        = frontier_params$xlim,
  show_band        = TRUE,
  verbose          = TRUE,

  # All other ForestSearch arguments — pass-through via ... .
  # These match the single-rule analysis chunks 1-for-1 except for
  # sg_focus and selection_rule (which the wrapper supplies).
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  outcome.name     = adverse_outcome,
  treat.name       = treat.name,
  id.name          = id.name,
  outcome_type     = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure   = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome  = TRUE,
  seedit           = analysis_seed,
  effect.threshold       = fs_md_threshold,
  consistency.threshold  = fs_md_consistency,
  pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency,
  max_subgroups_search = fs_max_subgroups,
  use_twostage     = TRUE,
  conf.cont_jcuts  = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  use_grf          = fs_use_grf,
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,
  use_lasso        = fs_use_lasso,
  cut_type         = "default",
  maxk             = fs_maxk,
  n.min            = fs_n_min,
  d0.min           = fs_d0_min,
  d1.min           = fs_d1_min,
  fs.splits        = fs_splits,
  parallel_args    = list(
    plan         = "multisession",
    workers      = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  show_candidate_summary = TRUE,
  details          = TRUE,
  plot.sg          = FALSE,
  is.RCT           = fs_is_RCT,
  vi.grf.min       = fs_vi_grf_min,
  dmin.grf         = fs_dmin_grf,
  cont.cutoff      = fs_cont_cutoff,
  tune_grf         = FALSE,
  quiet            = FALSE
)

5 Per-Combo Diagnostics

5.1 Captured Console Output

The wrapper captured the in-flight diagnostic output from each forestsearch() call. Each combination’s two diagnostic banners – the CANDIDATE EVALUATION PREVIEW (pre-consistency; all candidates entering evaluation) and the CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY (post-consistency; passing candidates with Pcons / Frontier / InBand / Selected flags) – are shown below as the primary view. The full captured output (GRF preview, Cox-LASSO selection, filtering summary, parallel-config messages, post-run timings, etc.) is folded into a collapsible block for readers who want the complete context.

Code 
# Loop over all combos.  This replaces the previous two hardcoded
# sub-sections so the document handles n_combos > 2 correctly
# (e.g. effMaxSG/pareto, effMaxSG/both, effMinSG/pareto, effMinSG/both).
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### %s\n\n", combo_labels[i]))

  diag <- comparison$diagnostics[[i]]

  cat("**Pre-consistency preview:**\n\n")
  if (!is.na(diag$preview)) {
    cat("```\n", diag$preview, "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("_(not available)_\n\n")
  }

  cat("**Post-consistency summary:**\n\n")
  if (!is.na(diag$summary)) {
    cat("```\n", diag$summary, "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("_(not available)_\n\n")
  }

  cat("<details><summary>Full forestsearch output (expand)</summary>\n\n```\n")
  cat(comparison$console[[i]], sep = "\n")
  cat("\n```\n\n</details>\n\n")
}

5.2 Pareto-Frontier Plots

Each combination produces its own Pareto frontier on (MD, N). The plot for each combo is shown individually below, then composed side-by-side via patchwork for direct visual comparison.

5.2.1 Individual Panels

Code 
print(comparison$plots[[1]])
Code 
print(comparison$plots[[2]])

5.2.2 Side-by-Side Composition

Code 
print(comparison$plot_grid)

5.3 Combined Plot(s) by Matching Passing-Set Group

compare_selection_rules() groups configurations by their post-consistency passing set. When all configurations share one passing set, a single combined plot is built (comparison$plot_combined). When configurations fall into two or more matching groups – e.g. all effMaxSG runs agree, all effMinSG runs agree, but the two sg_focus values disagree on which candidates pass – a combined plot is built per group and stored in comparison$plot_combined_subsets. Each group’s plot labels its selected subgroups with S<i>: markers identifying the configuration(s) that picked them.

Code 
if (!is.null(comparison$plot_combined)) {
  cat("All configurations share one passing set; single combined plot:\n\n")
  print(comparison$plot_combined)
} else if (length(comparison$plot_combined_subsets) > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf("Passing sets fall into %d matching group(s); one combined plot per group:\n\n",
              length(comparison$plot_combined_subsets)))
  for (nm in names(comparison$plot_combined_subsets)) {
    cat(sprintf("Group: %s\n", nm))
    print(comparison$plot_combined_subsets[[nm]])
  }
  if (!is.null(comparison$combined_skip_reason)) {
    cat("\nNote: ", comparison$combined_skip_reason, "\n", sep = "")
  }
} else {
  cat("**No combined plot.**\n\n")
  if (!is.null(comparison$combined_skip_reason)) {
    cat("Reason:  ", comparison$combined_skip_reason, "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("See the side-by-side composition above as the alternative view.\n")
}
Passing sets fall into 2 matching group(s); one combined plot per group:

Group: effMinSG
Group: effMaxSG

5.4 Frontier Tables

Per-combination Pareto-frontier table with split-derived and FSBC CIs. Selected subgroup is highlighted with ★.

Code 
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", combo_labels[i]))
  tbl <- pareto_frontier_table(
    comparison$fs[[i]],
    ci_table = comparison$ci_tab[[i]],
    digits   = frontier_params$digits
  )
  print(tbl)
  cat("\n\n")
}

5.5 Selection Narratives

explain_pareto_selection() produces a verbal account of why the selected subgroup wins on the configured lexicographic criterion relative to the other non-dominated candidates. Reading the two narratives together highlights which axis of the lex key the two rules tie-broke on differently.

Code 
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", combo_labels[i]))
  cat(explain_pareto_selection(
    comparison$fs[[i]],
    ci_table = comparison$ci_tab[[i]],
    digits   = frontier_params$digits
  ))
  cat("\n\n")
}

5.5.1 effMaxSG / pareto

Selection criterion. The configured criterion is largest-N among non-dominated candidates (sg_focus = “hrMaxSG”) under the Pareto-non-dominance rule. Within the eligible set, ties on N are broken by Pcons, then by effect strength, then by parsimony (smaller K).

Selected subgroup. !{cd40 <= 396} AND !{wtkg <= 78.1} (mean difference = 58.09, N = 122, Pcons = 0.92, K = 2). This is the largest-N candidate in the eligible set among non-dominated frontier candidates. The Naive 95% CI for the mean difference on this subgroup is (3.17, 113.01).

Non-selected frontier candidates (ordered by closeness to winning):

  • {age <= 35.2} AND !{cd40 <= 449} (mean difference = 66.40, N = 110, Pcons = 0.97, K = 2). Smaller subgroup (N=110 vs N=122, 12 fewer subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker among non-dominated candidates, so this candidate’s stronger effect could not overcome the size loss.

  • {age <= 34} AND !{cd40 <= 449} (mean difference = 71.34, N = 101, Pcons = 0.95, K = 2). Smaller subgroup (N=101 vs N=122, 21 fewer subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker among non-dominated candidates, so this candidate’s stronger effect could not overcome the size loss.

  • !{cd40 <= 396} AND !{wtkg <= 81.2} (mean difference = 76.58, N = 99, Pcons = 0.99, K = 2). Smaller subgroup (N=99 vs N=122, 23 fewer subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker among non-dominated candidates, so this candidate’s stronger effect could not overcome the size loss.

  • !{cd40 <= 396} AND !{wtkg <= 82.3284} (mean difference = 82.78, N = 87, Pcons = 0.97, K = 2). Smaller subgroup (N=87 vs N=122, 35 fewer subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker among non-dominated candidates, so this candidate’s stronger effect could not overcome the size loss.

  • !{cd40 <= 506.6} AND {age <= 35.2} (mean difference = 85.92, N = 61, Pcons = 0.91, K = 2). Smaller subgroup (N=61 vs N=122, 61 fewer subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker among non-dominated candidates, so this candidate’s stronger effect could not overcome the size loss.

5.5.2 effMaxSG / both

Selection criterion. The configured criterion is largest-N within the effect-size band (sg_focus = “hrMaxSG”) under the intersection of effect-band and Pareto-non-dominance rules. The effect-size band requires mean difference within 10% of the maximum on the frontier (i.e., mean difference >= 77.32). Within the eligible set, ties on N are broken by Pcons, then by effect strength, then by parsimony (smaller K).

Selected subgroup. !{cd40 <= 396} AND !{wtkg <= 82.3284} (mean difference = 82.78, N = 87, Pcons = 0.99, K = 2). This is the largest-N candidate in the eligible set among non-dominated frontier candidates. The Naive 95% CI for the mean difference on this subgroup is (14.81, 150.76).

Non-selected frontier candidates (ordered by closeness to winning):

  • !{cd40 <= 506.6} AND {age <= 35.2} (mean difference = 85.92, N = 61, Pcons = 0.99, K = 2). Smaller subgroup (N=61 vs N=87, 26 fewer subjects). N is the primary tiebreaker once the band is satisfied, so this candidate’s stronger effect could not overcome the size loss.

  • !{cd40 <= 396} AND !{wtkg <= 81.2} (mean difference = 76.58, N = 99, Pcons = 0.99, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (mean difference = 76.58 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • {age <= 34} AND !{cd40 <= 449} (mean difference = 71.34, N = 101, Pcons = 0.96, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (mean difference = 71.34 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • {age <= 35.2} AND !{cd40 <= 449} (mean difference = 66.40, N = 110, Pcons = 0.95, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (mean difference = 66.40 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{cd40 <= 396} AND !{wtkg <= 78.1} (mean difference = 58.09, N = 122, Pcons = 0.92, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (mean difference = 58.09 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

6 Rich Post-Consistency View

The include_dominated = TRUE argument to pareto_frontier_table() shows all passing candidates (not just the frontier), with on_frontier and in_band flag columns added. This is the post-hoc analog of the CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY banner printed during the run.

Code 
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", combo_labels[i]))
  tbl <- pareto_frontier_table(
    comparison$fs[[i]],
    ci_table          = comparison$ci_tab[[i]],
    include_dominated = TRUE,
    digits            = frontier_params$digits
  )
  print(tbl)
  cat("\n\n")
}

comparison$diagnostics[[1]]$summary  # SUMMARY block as single string
comparison$diagnostics[[1]]$full     # entire captured stdout (single string)

comparison$errors[[1]]

# Introduction

This vignette compares the selection diagnostic side-by-side across two
choices of `selection_rule`, holding all other ForestSearch parameters
fixed.  It uses the package's
[`compare_selection_rules()`](../R/compare_selection_rules.R) wrapper to
run `forestsearch()` once per combination and bundle the per-combo
diagnostics for inspection.

The structure is:

1. **Data setup + ITT** — identical to the single-rule analyses.
2. **Comparison run** — one call to `compare_selection_rules()` that
   handles the loop, captures each run's
   `CANDIDATE EVALUATION PREVIEW` + `CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY`
   banners, builds the Pareto-frontier plots, and computes split-derived
   CIs.
3. **Per-combo diagnostics** — replay of captured console output,
   individual frontier plot/table/narrative for each combination.
4. **Side-by-side composition** — patchwork-composed plot panel
   for direct visual comparison.

Bootstrap, cross-validation, and the combined forest plot are
**deliberately omitted** so the document stays focused on the
*selection mechanism* and the comparison reads as a tight diagnostic
of the rule axis alone.


# Setup

## Load Required Packages

```{r load-packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(forestsearch)
  library(speff2trial)       # ACTG175 dataset
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gt)
  library(future)
  library(patchwork)         # for side-by-side plot composition
})

# Source the comparison wrapper.  When this graduates into the package
# (copy compare_selection_rules.R into R/ and run devtools::document()),
# this source() line can be removed.
#source("compare_selection_rules.R")

# Set ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```


## Analysis Parameters

All ForestSearch parameters are defined here once and reused for both
combinations.  The two axes of variation are `sg_focus` and
`selection_rule`, which the wrapper handles directly.

```{r analysis-params}
#| code-fold: false

# ─── Parallel processing ────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_cores <- max(1L, floor(0.95 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))

# ─── Reproducibility ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
analysis_seed <- 8316951L
set.seed(analysis_seed)

# ─── Confounders ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")
confounders.name <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)
id.name <- "id"

# ─── Variables (dual-scale framing) ────────────────────────────────────
treat.name         <- "treat"
adverse_outcome    <- "y_decline"   # FS adverse-scale outcome
beneficial_outcome <- "y_improve"   # GRF beneficial-scale outcome

# ─── ForestSearch parameters (continuous, MD scale) ────────────────────
fs_outcome_type    <- "continuous"
fs_effect_measure  <- "MD"

# NOTE: fs_sg_focus and fs_selection_rule are NOT defined here.
# They live in the `comparison-axes` chunk below as the two axes the
# wrapper varies.  All OTHER ForestSearch parameters are fixed across
# the comparison.

# Thresholds in CD4 count units (adverse scale: MD > c1 = harm)
fs_md_threshold    <- 10    # screening: MD >= 10 indicates harm
fs_md_consistency  <- 5     # consistency: MD >= 5

fs_pconsistency    <- 0.90
fs_n_min           <- 60L
fs_d0_min          <- 10L
fs_d1_min          <- 10L
fs_splits          <- 500L

fs_max_subgroups   <- 30

fs_maxk            <- 2L
fs_use_lasso       <- TRUE
fs_use_grf         <- TRUE
fs_is_RCT          <- TRUE
fs_vi_grf_min      <- -0.2
fs_dmin_grf        <- 0
fs_cont_cutoff     <- 4L

# ─── Pareto-frontier diagnostic parameters ──────────────────────────────
frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits      = 1000L,
  seed          = 1L,
  xlim          = NULL,
  digits        = 2L
)

# ─── Output directory for saved artifacts ───────────────────────────────
# .rds bundles (tidy selected-subgroups + full comparison object) are
# written by the "Selected Subgroups" section below.  Resolved relative
# to *this qmd's directory*, not the caller's getwd() -- so the path is
# the same whether the chunk is rendered by Quarto or executed
# interactively from a different working directory.  Created if it
# doesn't exist.  Matches the calibration-suite convention.
#
# Resolution: knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE) returns the full path
# of the input document during a render; NULL otherwise.  When NULL
# (e.g., interactive chunk execution), fall back to getwd(), which
# matches Quarto's behavior of cd'ing to the qmd's directory before
# rendering chunks.
qmd_input  <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
qmd_dir    <- if (is.null(qmd_input)) getwd() else dirname(qmd_input)
output_dir <- file.path(qmd_dir, "_data")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```


## Comparison Axes

The two axes varied by the wrapper.  Tuple semantics: paired
element-by-element.

::: {.callout-note}
**`sg_focus = "effMaxSG"` notation.**  The `"eff*"` names
(`"eff"`, `"effMaxSG"`, `"effMinSG"`) are GLM-natural aliases for
the legacy Cox-flavored names (`"hr"`, `"hrMaxSG"`, `"hrMinSG"`).
Both vocabularies produce identical results.  The `"eff*"` forms
read more naturally for continuous (MD), binary (OR/RR/RD), and
count (IRR) outcomes where there is no hazard ratio.  Old code
using `"hrMaxSG"` continues to work without changes.
:::

```{r comparison-axes}
sg_focus_vec       <- c("effMaxSG", "effMaxSG", "effMinSG", "effMinSG", "eff", "maxSG","minSG")
selection_rule_vec <- c("pareto",   "both", "pareto", "both", "neighborhood", "neighborhood", "neighborhood")

# Pretty labels used in plot titles, list names, and prose
combo_labels       <- paste(sg_focus_vec, selection_rule_vec, sep = " / ")
n_combos           <- length(sg_focus_vec)

cat("Combinations to be run:\n")
print(data.frame(
  combo          = seq_len(n_combos),
  sg_focus       = sg_focus_vec,
  selection_rule = selection_rule_vec,
  label          = combo_labels
))
```


# Data Preparation

## Treatment Assignment

```{r data-treat}
# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)
```


## Outcome Construction

```{r data-outcomes}
# Drop subjects missing the week-20 CD4 measurement
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# Adverse scale: CD4 decline (higher = worse)
actg_df$y_decline <- actg_df$cd40 - actg_df$cd420

outcome_vars <- c("y_decline")
```


## Covariates

```{r data-covariates}
# Coerce binary indicators to factors (analyst does not know true cuts
# for continuous covariates; ForestSearch handles those internally)
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.factor(actg_df[[v]])

cat("Continuous candidates:", paste(cont_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Binary candidates:    ", paste(bin_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Analysis N:", nrow(actg_df), "\n")
```


## Baseline Characteristics

```{r baseline-table}
create_summary_table(
  data             = actg_df,
  treat_var        = treat.name,
  table_title      = "ACTG175 Baseline Characteristics and Outcomes by Treatment Arm",
  vars_continuous  = c(outcome_vars, cont_vars),
  vars_categorical = bin_vars,
  font_size        = 12
)
```


## ITT Analysis

```{r itt-analysis}
itt_decline <- lm(y_decline ~ treat, data = actg_df)
cat("=== ITT Mean Difference, adverse scale (y_decline) ===\n")
print(summary(itt_decline)$coefficients["treat", , drop = FALSE])
```


# Selection-Rule Comparison

## Running `compare_selection_rules()`

One call to the wrapper runs `forestsearch()` for each
`(sg_focus, selection_rule)` combination with all other parameters
held fixed, and bundles the per-combo diagnostics into a single
object.

```{r run-comparison}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

t0 <- proc.time()

comparison <- compare_selection_rules(
  df.analysis      = actg_df,
  sg_focus         = sg_focus_vec,
  selection_rule   = selection_rule_vec,
  combo_labels     = combo_labels,

  # Wrapper-specific controls
  compute_cis      = TRUE,
  n_splits         = frontier_params$n_splits,
  ci_seed          = frontier_params$seed,
  plot_xlim        = frontier_params$xlim,
  show_band        = TRUE,
  verbose          = TRUE,

  # All other ForestSearch arguments — pass-through via ... .
  # These match the single-rule analysis chunks 1-for-1 except for
  # sg_focus and selection_rule (which the wrapper supplies).
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  outcome.name     = adverse_outcome,
  treat.name       = treat.name,
  id.name          = id.name,
  outcome_type     = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure   = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome  = TRUE,
  seedit           = analysis_seed,
  effect.threshold       = fs_md_threshold,
  consistency.threshold  = fs_md_consistency,
  pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency,
  max_subgroups_search = fs_max_subgroups,
  use_twostage     = TRUE,
  conf.cont_jcuts  = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  use_grf          = fs_use_grf,
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,
  use_lasso        = fs_use_lasso,
  cut_type         = "default",
  maxk             = fs_maxk,
  n.min            = fs_n_min,
  d0.min           = fs_d0_min,
  d1.min           = fs_d1_min,
  fs.splits        = fs_splits,
  parallel_args    = list(
    plan         = "multisession",
    workers      = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  ),
  show_candidate_summary = TRUE,
  details          = TRUE,
  plot.sg          = FALSE,
  is.RCT           = fs_is_RCT,
  vi.grf.min       = fs_vi_grf_min,
  dmin.grf         = fs_dmin_grf,
  cont.cutoff      = fs_cont_cutoff,
  tune_grf         = FALSE,
  quiet            = FALSE
)

plan("sequential"); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
timings$compare <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

cat("\nComparison completed in",
    round(timings$compare / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
```


## Comparison Summary

```{r comparison-summary}
print(comparison)
```


# Per-Combo Diagnostics

## Captured Console Output

The wrapper captured the in-flight diagnostic output from each
`forestsearch()` call.  Each combination's two diagnostic banners --
the `CANDIDATE EVALUATION PREVIEW` (pre-consistency; all candidates
entering evaluation) and the `CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY`
(post-consistency; passing candidates with
Pcons / Frontier / InBand / Selected flags) -- are shown below as the
primary view.  The full captured output (GRF preview, Cox-LASSO
selection, filtering summary, parallel-config messages, post-run
timings, etc.) is folded into a collapsible block for readers who want
the complete context.

```{r console-loop, results = "asis"}
# Loop over all combos.  This replaces the previous two hardcoded
# sub-sections so the document handles n_combos > 2 correctly
# (e.g. effMaxSG/pareto, effMaxSG/both, effMinSG/pareto, effMinSG/both).
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### %s\n\n", combo_labels[i]))

  diag <- comparison$diagnostics[[i]]

  cat("**Pre-consistency preview:**\n\n")
  if (!is.na(diag$preview)) {
    cat("```\n", diag$preview, "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("_(not available)_\n\n")
  }

  cat("**Post-consistency summary:**\n\n")
  if (!is.na(diag$summary)) {
    cat("```\n", diag$summary, "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("_(not available)_\n\n")
  }

  cat("<details><summary>Full forestsearch output (expand)</summary>\n\n```\n")
  cat(comparison$console[[i]], sep = "\n")
  cat("\n```\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```


## Pareto-Frontier Plots

Each combination produces its own Pareto frontier on (MD, N).  The
plot for each combo is shown individually below, then composed
side-by-side via `patchwork` for direct visual comparison.

### Individual Panels

```{r plot-combo-1}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: !expr sprintf("Pareto frontier — %s", combo_labels[1])

print(comparison$plots[[1]])
```


```{r plot-combo-2}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: !expr sprintf("Pareto frontier — %s", combo_labels[2])

print(comparison$plots[[2]])
```


### Side-by-Side Composition

```{r plot-side-by-side}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Pareto frontier across selection rules (side-by-side)"

print(comparison$plot_grid)
```


## Combined Plot(s) by Matching Passing-Set Group

`compare_selection_rules()` groups configurations by their
post-consistency passing set.  When all configurations share one
passing set, a single combined plot is built (`comparison$plot_combined`).
When configurations fall into two or more matching groups -- e.g. all
`effMaxSG` runs agree, all `effMinSG` runs agree, but the two
`sg_focus` values disagree on which candidates pass -- a combined plot
is built per group and stored in `comparison$plot_combined_subsets`.
Each group's plot labels its selected subgroups with `S<i>:` markers
identifying the configuration(s) that picked them.

```{r plot-combined}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Combined Pareto frontier with S1/S2 winner annotations"

if (!is.null(comparison$plot_combined)) {
  cat("All configurations share one passing set; single combined plot:\n\n")
  print(comparison$plot_combined)
} else if (length(comparison$plot_combined_subsets) > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf("Passing sets fall into %d matching group(s); one combined plot per group:\n\n",
              length(comparison$plot_combined_subsets)))
  for (nm in names(comparison$plot_combined_subsets)) {
    cat(sprintf("Group: %s\n", nm))
    print(comparison$plot_combined_subsets[[nm]])
  }
  if (!is.null(comparison$combined_skip_reason)) {
    cat("\nNote: ", comparison$combined_skip_reason, "\n", sep = "")
  }
} else {
  cat("**No combined plot.**\n\n")
  if (!is.null(comparison$combined_skip_reason)) {
    cat("Reason:  ", comparison$combined_skip_reason, "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("See the side-by-side composition above as the alternative view.\n")
}
```


## Frontier Tables

Per-combination Pareto-frontier table with split-derived and FSBC
CIs.  Selected subgroup is highlighted with ★.

```{r table-combo-loop, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", combo_labels[i]))
  tbl <- pareto_frontier_table(
    comparison$fs[[i]],
    ci_table = comparison$ci_tab[[i]],
    digits   = frontier_params$digits
  )
  print(tbl)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```


## Selection Narratives

`explain_pareto_selection()` produces a verbal account of why the
selected subgroup wins on the configured lexicographic criterion
relative to the other non-dominated candidates.  Reading the two
narratives together highlights which axis of the lex key the two
rules tie-broke on differently.

```{r explain-loop, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", combo_labels[i]))
  cat(explain_pareto_selection(
    comparison$fs[[i]],
    ci_table = comparison$ci_tab[[i]],
    digits   = frontier_params$digits
  ))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```


# Rich Post-Consistency View

The `include_dominated = TRUE` argument to `pareto_frontier_table()`
shows **all** passing candidates (not just the frontier), with
`on_frontier` and `in_band` flag columns added.  This is the
post-hoc analog of the `CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY` banner printed
during the run.

```{r dominated-loop, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_len(n_combos)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s`\n\n", combo_labels[i]))
  tbl <- pareto_frontier_table(
    comparison$fs[[i]],
    ci_table          = comparison$ci_tab[[i]],
    include_dominated = TRUE,
    digits            = frontier_params$digits
  )
  print(tbl)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```


# Programmatic Access (Reference)

```{r programmatic, eval = FALSE}
# Each combination's full fs object is available for downstream use.
# Index with [[i]] where i runs from 1 to n_combos; see comparison$combos
# for the (sg_focus, selection_rule, label) tuple at each index.
comparison$combos                    # data.frame: per-combo configuration
comparison$fs[[1]]                   # fs object for combo 1

# CI tables (data.tables, one per combo):
comparison$ci_tab[[1]]

# Plot objects (ggplot, one per combo):
comparison$plots[[1]]

# Side-by-side panel (single patchwork object):
comparison$plot_grid

# Combined plot (when passing sets match), and the reason if skipped:
comparison$plot_combined             # ggplot or NULL (all combos match)
comparison$plot_combined_subsets     # named list of ggplots, one per
                                     # matching subset of size >= 2
comparison$combined_skip_reason      # character or NULL

# Console output (full captured stdout, one character per line):
comparison$console[[1]]

# Diagnostics (filtered slices: preview, summary, full):
comparison$diagnostics[[1]]$preview  # PREVIEW block as single string
comparison$diagnostics[[1]]$summary  # SUMMARY block as single string
comparison$diagnostics[[1]]$full     # entire captured stdout (single string)

# Errors (NULL if combo succeeded):
comparison$errors[[1]]
```


# Selected Subgroups (Tidy Summary)

`extract_selected_subgroups()` reduces the per-combo results to a tidy
one-row-per-configuration data.frame.  Saved to disk below so a separate
post-hoc document can `rbind()` this analysis's summary with a binary
or count analysis's summary into a single side-by-side table.

```{r selected-subgroups-tidy}
selected_tidy <- extract_selected_subgroups(comparison,
                                            analysis_label = "continuous")
selected_tidy
```

```{r selected-subgroups-gt}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)

# Compact gt rendering: drop columns that are uniform within an analysis
# (outcome_type, effect_measure) and the error column (NA on success).
disp_cols <- setdiff(
  names(selected_tidy),
  c("outcome_type", "effect_measure", "error", "analysis")
)
gt::gt(selected_tidy[, disp_cols, drop = FALSE]) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Selected Subgroups Across Configurations",
    subtitle = sprintf("Continuous outcome (effect = %s)",
                       unique(stats::na.omit(selected_tidy$effect_measure)))
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("effect", "Pcons"), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—")
```

```{r save-comparison-artifact}
#| code-fold: false

# Persist both (a) the tidy selected-subgroups summary -- compact, easy
# to read across documents -- and (b) the full comparison object for
# anyone who needs to drill into per-combo plots, CIs, or captured
# diagnostics in the post-hoc document.
# Destination is `output_dir` (defined in the analysis-params chunk at
# the top of this document).
saveRDS(selected_tidy,
        file = file.path(output_dir, "selected_subgroups_continuous.rds"))
saveRDS(comparison,
        file = file.path(output_dir, "comparison_continuous.rds"))

cat("Output directory: ", normalizePath(output_dir), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Saved tidy summary:        selected_subgroups_continuous.rds\n")
cat("Saved full comparison:     comparison_continuous.rds\n")
cat(sprintf("(tidy rows: %d; comparison combos: %d)\n",
            nrow(selected_tidy), nrow(comparison$combos)))
```


# Computational Timing

```{r timing-summary}
timings$total <- (proc.time() - t_doc_start)["elapsed"]

timing_df <- data.frame(
  Component = c(sprintf("Comparison run (%d combos)", n_combos),
                "Total document"),
  Seconds   = c(timings$compare, timings$total)
)
timing_df$Minutes <- timing_df$Seconds / 60

gt(timing_df) |>
  tab_header(title = "Computational Timing") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Seconds, Minutes), decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(
    Component = "Component",
    Seconds   = "Time (sec)",
    Minutes   = "Time (min)"
  )
```
